method: VM presentation lifecycle, native callback observers and canvas contract; fake images; not raster/gameplay approval

checks.name: Cold image preserves the warning without old glyph, texture flood or legacy renderer

Charge trail stops at its actual collision endpoint rather than its telegraphed maximum
Dead owner and delayed hazards cannot draw or fabricate release material
Real heal callback records the recipient coordinate; old state/resources/RNG are read only
Only the native flute release tags its new moving shots; resident fan stays inherited
Each animated flute collision core remains exactly on the physical shot position
Antenna fixed content bounds reach both actual beam endpoints while preserving its clip
Fixed cone content bounds occupy the native useful sector without changing alpha or per-frame scale
Actual native contact uses the last real projectile position; expiry and arbitrary clear do not impact
Native Coro melee is an immediate scoped cosmetic event, not a new attack timer
Summon condensation follows only actual spawned minions and their original timer
Coro uses one fixed authored ground base so healing grows above the recipient anchor
Maestro emergence keeps its authored base fixed throughout original spawn phases
Pause freezes cosmetic time; area and game reset remove effects and projectile ownership
Sprite budget is bounded while dangerous projectiles retain a visible collision core
Only the fresh exact native release decoration is hidden; original list identity and data restore after paint
Scoped suppression restores the original list even when the delegate throws
Foreign decorations appended during delegated drawing survive scoped suppression
Maestro hides spawn decoration only for new real owned minions and preserves other spawns
Charge hides only its fresh terminal strike after the actual recovery callback
Maestro native intra-frame spawn aging is exact at dt=0.01; foreign age0.2 remains visible
Maestro native intra-frame spawn aging is exact at dt=0.05; foreign age0.2 remains visible
Release holds two full-alpha peak frames for180ms, then fades through450ms without extending damage
Corporeal flight has a long raster body and keeps all measured core anchors on collision
V2 flight registration can replace V1 pivots without moving the physical projectile
Recipient healing is painted once in overlay, leaving the entire ground pass free of its column
Reduced motion fixes the peak pose but still removes release material at450ms
Frozen V2 PNG geometry and measured flight pivots register all three physical cores
